research_status.statement: This expansion is conceptual. No source retrieval, primary-source reading, literature survey, empirical case study or novelty finding is claimed.

tests.question: Does the set-inclusion rule entail preservation, strict improvement, transitivity, asymmetry and incomparability exactly as claimed?
tests.method: Enumerate met-sets over a finite obligation universe, including all triples; separately enumerate task-switching chains and identify which inference fails when T changes.
tests.evidence_required: Reproducible derivation or small exhaustive program with the exact fixed-T assumptions and counterexamples for cross-task inference.
tests.decision_rule: If any fixed-T cycle or loss of a previously met obligation is derivable under the definitions, reject or repair the rule; do not relax the task identity condition silently.

tests.question: Can the task profile be justified without seeing which standard it favors?
tests.method: Have a separate assessor specify uses, obligations, thresholds, and evidence rules from the task description while blinded to candidate identities and scores; reveal candidate results only after sealing the profile. Repeat with reasonable rival task framings.
tests.evidence_required: Sealed precomparison profile, its rationale, assessor disagreement, and sensitivity results across plausible profiles.
tests.decision_rule: If the verdict depends on retrospective task choice or plausible rival profiles reverse it, report conditional judgments or suspend comparison.

tests.question: Does the replacement preserve previously warranted outcomes and resolve a stated failure beyond the cases used to design it?
tests.method: Preselect shared and held-out cases, score both standards under identical evidence rules, and record unknowns and new failures rather than mapping them to success.
tests.evidence_required: Exact case set, task registry, output snapshots, scoring rationale, and complete pass/fail/unknown matrix.
tests.decision_rule: Claim strict improvement only if the new met-set is a strict superset over the registered complete comparison set. Otherwise report trade-off, incomparability, or failure.

tests.question: Do existing primary accounts of measurement, scientific progress, or conceptual change already use a plural task-relative relation equivalent to this rule?
tests.method: Retrieve and read primary works on measurement standards and scientific progress/conceptual change; trace cited sources from the closest passages; reconstruct each account before comparing its relation, task invariance, treatment of trade-offs, and cycle conditions.
tests.evidence_required: Saved exact source bytes, retrieval log, precise full/excerpt coverage, and a claim-by-claim source comparison. Bibliographic metadata alone is insufficient.
tests.decision_rule: Keep originality UNKNOWN until the closest comparison is completed. If an existing account already supplies the same relation, identify a defensible difference or set aside any originality claim.

tests.question: Can a documented historical change in measurement standard meet the fixed-profile conditions without retrospective task selection?
tests.method: Choose one case only after source inventory; identify contemporaneous task commitments and the original evidence, then compare standards using a profile justified independently of later success narratives.
tests.evidence_required: Primary records from both sides of the transition, source coverage manifest, and explicit treatment of missing evidence.
tests.decision_rule: If the profile is available only retrospectively or standards change the identity of the cases beyond defensible mapping, do not claim historical progress from this framework.

next_probe_inputs_needed: This exact proposal and argument-map.json only, plus its explicitly selected ancestral assessment inputs.
A separately prepared primary-source packet built after T4 retrieval, with exact bytes and honest coverage.
No other idea, proposal, essay, ranking, or unselected assessor report.
